stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Try each of the three modes — magnet ↔ magnet, magnet ↔ solenoid, wire ↔ wire. Flip the poles or current directions and watch how the interaction between $A$ and $B$ changes. Advance after you've tried all $3$ modes and seen both an attract and a repel result.
stages.concept: Magnets and current-carrying conductors interact through magnetic fields. Two magnets attract when opposite poles ($N \to S$) face each other, and repel when like poles face each other. A solenoid (coil) with current behaves like a bar magnet — the current direction sets which end is $N$ and which is $S$ (right-hand rule). Two parallel wires attract when their currents flow in the same direction, and repel when they flow in opposite directions.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: For each mode, configure $A$ and $B$ so the interaction matches the target shown at the bottom. Switch modes with the tabs on the right and mark all three targets ✓ to advance.
stages.concept: In each mode, apply the rule: same poles / same-direction currents $\Rightarrow$ repel; opposite poles / opposite-direction currents $\Rightarrow$ attract. For the solenoid, flipping the current effectively flips its $N$ / $S$ ends, so the same rule applies to it as to a bar magnet.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The interaction indicator is hidden. Look at the configuration shown, predict whether $A$ and $B$ will attract or repel, then click your answer to reveal the truth. Peek briefly reveals the correct arrows if you're stuck.
stages.concept: Read the configuration: identify the two facing poles (for magnets), or the two current directions (for wires). Same-facing $\Rightarrow$ repel; opposite-facing $\Rightarrow$ attract. For the solenoid: current direction $\to$ $N$ / $S$ ends via right-hand rule $\to$ compare with the magnet's facing pole.

labels.question: question
labels.predict_prompt: Predict the interaction between A and B, then click to reveal.
labels.tip1: try each mode; flip poles or current to see both outcomes
labels.tip2: one target per mode — switch modes with the tabs on the right
labels.tip3: guess first, then click; peek briefly reveals the truth

1.1: Use the mode tabs to switch between A↔A, A↔C, and C↔C. Try flipping A or B in each.
1.2: For magnets: same poles facing = repel, opposite = attract. For wires: same direction = attract, opposite = repel.
1.3: You need to visit all 3 modes and see at least one attract + one repel outcome. Flip a pole or current to change the outcome.

2.1: Switch modes on the right panel. Each mode has one target — try to hit them all.
2.2: aa: opposite poles attract. cc: same-direction currents attract. ac: N-face facing S-face attracts.
2.3: For ac (repel): flip the magnet or the current so the two facing poles are the SAME (N-N or S-S).

3.1: Look at the visible configuration. What are the two facing poles (or current directions)?
3.2: Same-facing = repel. Opposite-facing = attract. Peek briefly reveals the answer if you're stuck.
3.3: For a solenoid, apply the right-hand rule: curl fingers along current, thumb points to N. Then compare with the magnet's facing pole.
